transcript:
User: yeah.
Agent: Hey, this is Linda with Dialux — what made you call in today?
User: dunno, just checking.
Agent: Got it, you’re just kind of feeling it out.  

So how did you come across us — was it a voicemail from Jay, an ad, or were you just searching around online?
User: dunno, whatever's fine.
Agent: Totally fair, just browsing is fine.  

Quick check then — do you run a business where missed calls or voicemails might be costing you customers, or is that not really a concern for you right now?
User: dunno, maybe a little.
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense — even “a little” adds up over time.  

When someone calls your business and you *don’t* pick up, what usually happens next — do they leave a voicemail, call back later, or just disappear?
User: dunno, maybe they leave a voicemail or call back.
Agent: Gotcha, so it’s kind of a mix.  

When those calls do leave a voicemail, do you usually get back to them pretty quickly, or does it sometimes slip a day or two?
User: dunno, maybe quickly, maybe not.
Agent: Mhm, so it’s a bit hit or miss depending on the day.  

If you had to guess, are you missing just a couple calls a week, or is it more like “I have no idea how many I’m not picking up”?
User: dunno, maybe a couple or maybe more. Not sure.
Agent: Yeah, that uncertainty is super common.  

So just to check, do you actually run a business right now, or are you more just curious about what we do in general?
User: dunno, maybe a bit of both.
Agent: Gotcha, so you’re kind of curious *and* might have a use for it.  

So, very simply: are you more interested in getting more business from missed calls, or more interested in the tech itself and how it works?
User: dunno, maybe a bit interested in both. Not really sure about specifics.
Agent: Totally fine — you don’t need specifics yet.  

So, do you actually have people calling you today for work-related stuff (customers, clients, tenants, patients, anything like that), or not really?
User: dunno, maybe sometimes, but not too sure. Calls happen, you know.
Agent: Yeah, I hear you — calls just kind of come and go.  

Since you’re mostly just exploring, would it be helpful if I quickly explain, in plain English, what we actually do for businesses when they miss calls, and you can decide if it’s even relevant to you?
User: dunno, maybe. it's fine. whatever you think is best.
Agent: Gotcha, I can keep it simple.  

So, in plain terms, we stop you from losing money when you miss calls — instead of people hitting voicemail or giving up, our system answers, books appointments, and takes down real opportunities for you automatically; does that sound like something you’d even want *if* you are getting business calls?
User: dunno, maybe. sounds fine if useful. not sure about the specifics though.
Agent: Totally makes sense to not be sure on specifics yet.  

Tell me this: do you *want* more business or bookings from the calls you’re already getting, or is that not really a big priority for you right now?
User: dunno, maybe more business would be good, but it's not a big priority. whatever works, I guess.
Agent: Got it, so it’s a “nice to have” more than a must-have right now.  

Since it’s not a big priority, do you want to keep this as a quick info call today and leave it there, or would you actually want a short live walkthrough with Jay sometime to really see what it does and then decide later?
User: dunno, maybe just a quick info call. not sure about the walkthrough with Jay right now.
Agent: Makes sense, we can definitely keep it light.  

Since you’re in “just looking” mode, is there one thing you’re most curious about — how it works behind the scenes, what kinds of businesses use it, or what it roughly costs?
User: dunno, maybe how it works behind the scenes. not too sure about other stuff. whatever's fine.
Agent: Got it, let’s keep it simple then.  

Behind the scenes, when someone calls you and you can’t answer, our system picks up like a super-trained receptionist, talks with the caller in real time, answers basic questions, books appointments or takes messages, and then sends everything to you by text/email so you don’t lose the lead — does that level of automation sound too much, or actually kind of appealing if you *were* busier with calls?
User: dunno, maybe appealing if busier, but not sure. whatever works.
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense — it’s more of a “maybe later” thing if calls pick up.  

Since you’re just casually exploring, do you want me to send you a super short summary you can look at on your own time, or would you rather just leave it here for now?
User: maybe send a summary. or just leave it. whatever works. not in a rush, really.
Agent: Gotcha, you’re not in a rush and either way is fine.  

Since you’re pretty casual about it, why don’t we just leave it here for now — if your call volume ever picks up and you want to stop losing people when you miss a call, would you be open to chatting again then?
User: yeah, maybe. whenever's fine. not rushing. if it works out, it works out. whatever happens, happens.
Agent: Totally fair, we can just leave it open-ended for now. If your calls ever start picking up and you want to squeeze more business out of the ones you’re missing, you’re always welcome to reach back out and we can dive deeper then. Thanks for taking a few minutes with me today — have a good one.
